claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for launch on a disclosure-plus-monitoring basis despite an exposed below-target health-plan benefits support segment.
decision_criteria: If explicit pre-launch disclosure for the exposed named use case is evidenced, certification could be compliant on a disclosure-plus-monitoring basis.
If reviewed and approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed segment is evidenced, certification could also be compliant.
Without disclosed limitation or approved risk acceptance, exposed rollout plus known below-target performance fails the stated policy threshold.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual launch documentation or model card showing explicit disclosure of the benefits-eligibility explanation limitation for the named health-plan benefits support use case.
Provide an approved risk-acceptance record, if any, that specifically addresses continued exposure of the health-plan benefits support segment.
Provide the certification artifact or approval packet demonstrating the disclosure predicate was satisfied before launch.
specific_concerns: The affected health-plan benefits support segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
Policy text says rollout controls and monitoring are insufficient when the affected segment remains exposed unless there is reviewed risk acceptance or disclosure duty is satisfied.
The cited risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, unapproved, and does not address the exposed segment.
There is no admissible evidence that the required limitation disclosure is actually present in launch documentation or certification materials.
The actor's packet shifts from evidence of current state to a conditional rationale for what would make certification supportable.
unsupported_claims: The strongest admissible basis for certification is explicit launch disclosure of the limitation plus monitoring and rollback controls.
Certification is supportable on the present record, because no admissible evidence shows the required disclosure has actually been made.
